method: The capture program imports and calls the actual old detector packages.
Controlled io.ReadCloser instances record Open/Read/Close counts and inject open/read/close failures.
Successful profiles are serialized by the actual old MarshalSnapshot functions.
No production function was copied or reimplemented in the capture.
All bytes are small generated public fixtures; 1 MiB ONS boundary data is generated deterministically.
compatibilityFacts: ONS reads at most exactly 1 MiB and ignores bytes after that bound.
ONS DAT markers do not open a resource.
All three old detectors ignore Close errors after successful reads.
Butterscotch and NXEngine accept fixed prefixes even when physical bytes are shorter than declared descriptors.
NXEngine probes the EXE before checking required assets.
A nil reader returned with nil error panics in each old detector; later adapter fail-closed handling is explicitly a new boundary.
